title: Co-op Roguelike with Skill Trees, Procedural dungeons & Epic loot
author: sharkymcstevenson2
selftext:
Showing my latest co-op roguelike build that includes 6 different procedural map biomes and dungeons, skill tree with different character paths that goes to level 20, a transparent diablo-style overlay map and some pretty neat fighting! 

Video shows me playing the game w my friend

**This was the 3 first prompts:**

1.⁠ ⁠Core game

Build a Path of Exile-style action RPG where I fight large enemy packs using powerful abilities, level up my skills, and explore procedurally generated dungeons with unlimited rooms.

2.⁠ ⁠Loot and inventory

Add gear drops, weapon pickups, an inventory system with stat upgrades, and a Path of Exile-style map overlay opened with Tab. Give the top-down dungeon more visual depth and atmosphere.

3.⁠ ⁠Expanded dungeon progression

Procedural dungeon maps: code-authored floors and walls, varied environments as players descend, treasure chests, more weapons, new enemy types and larger packs, plus a skill tree for unlocking and upgrading abilities.

comments.author: PaintingThat7623
comments.body: Those were your \*actual\* 3 prompts? How is that possible, what are you using? I must've prompted couple hundred times over last months to achieve something very similar that you have.

replies.author: sharkymcstevenson2
replies.body:
Yessir! This was done entirely on tesana, using their atomos model: [https://tesana.ai/en/blog/introducing-atomos](https://tesana.ai/en/blog/introducing-atomos)

before the prompts, I had some reference images I inputted to get the art style like I wanted

replies.author: PaintingThat7623
replies.body:
You gotta be kidding me. Reading about this now and it looks unbelievable.

I have a very good reference because I'm making something very simillar with Codex, and to put it in perspective - mine had a 30 page GDD transformed into a 60 task plan and ran for about a month, requiring tens or hundreds of prompts to steer the ai despite the *very* detailed plan.

Holy shit, if this actually works - thank you!

replies.author: sharkymcstevenson2
replies.body:
Oufff that sounds painful haha, yeah you need to work on game-specific models or you'll have to do alot of the heavy lifting yourself, and it barely works even then. 

My workflow for this build started with prompt 1 (the core prompt), + my reference image for the style I was going for - I let tesana build out the game plan, approved it once I was happy with it, and then iterated from there with the following prompts :)
